componentPlan.focusQuote: Of the many processes involved in the hydrologic cycle, the most important are:
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Models the cycle in taught order so learners can trace how water moves through each stage

componentPlan.focusQuote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Connects named cycle parts to the diagram so learners can locate each process in the image

overview.headline: Continuous circulation of water between Earth and atmosphere

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the water cycle moves water from the ground to the atmosphere and back again.
keyPoints.quote: At its core, the water cycle is the motion of the water from the ground to the atmosphere and back again.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that transpiration carries water from plants through stomata into the atmosphere.
keyPoints.quote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that condensation is the process where water vapor is changed into a liquid state.
keyPoints.quote: Condensation is the process whereby water vapor is changed into a liquid state.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that precipitation falls to Earth after condensation particles grow too large for rising air.
keyPoints.quote: tiny condensation particles, through collision and coalescence, grow too large for the rising air to support

keyTerms.gloss: Change of state from liquid water to vapor gas
keyTerms.quote: Evaporation is the change of state in a substance from a liquid to a gas.

keyTerms.gloss: Evaporation of water from plants through leaves
keyTerms.quote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.

keyTerms.gloss: Process where water vapor is changed into liquid
keyTerms.quote: Condensation is the process whereby water vapor is changed into a liquid state.

keyTerms.gloss: Falling water in the form of rain, hail, snow or sleet
keyTerms.quote: Precipitation can be in the form of rain, hail, snow, or sleet.

keyTerms.gloss: Excess precipitation flowing over saturated ground
keyTerms.quote: Runoff occurs when there is excessive precipitation and the ground is saturated (cannot absorb any more water).

analysis.pageCoverage: The page explains the hydrologic cycle, describing evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation and runoff and how water moves between ground, plants, atmosphere and oceans.
analysis.subject: earth-science
